title: ask_simulation -- AM (experiment) asks BD (simulation)
description: Carries dimensional primitives in the units they were measured in, plus the assumption declaration. It does NOT carry dimensionless groups: AM does not nondimensionalise, BD does (README rule W1).

plan_ref.description: The local plan this ask was distilled from. The plan itself does not cross.

claim.description: A falsifiable statement, not a setting. 'objective = 100x' is not a claim.

system_primitives.description: Measured/handbook primitives ONLY. Composites (gamma, tau_k, f_c, D, ...) belong in reference_only -- validator rule R3. Rationale: 3*pi*eta*d and 6*pi*eta*a are the same formula, and sending the composite is where the factor-of-2 enters silently (BD intake ambiguity A1).

instrument_envelope.description: What the instrument can actually do, as ranges. Lets BD answer 'your camera cannot reach this' instead of proposing something unbuildable.

reference_only.description: NON-BINDING. Numbers AM derived in its own gates. BD must derive its own first and compare afterwards -- order matters, it is what keeps this a signal rather than an anchor.

items.description: This document corrects a PREVIOUS round of its own side. It therefore speaks out of turn: round parity (odd = experiment, even = simulation) does not hold for a correction, because the side that discovers its own earlier answer was wrong is the only side that can say so. Observed 2026-09-15: BD found r2's +1.17 % to be an estimator bias rather than physics, while AM was already drafting r3 against it.

what.description: Which field of the corrected document is wrong.

downstream.description: Everything that rests on the wrong value and must be revisited. A correction that does not name its dependents leaves them silently wrong.

kind.description:
What sort of gap this is, because `would_need` collapses kinds that send a reader to different places.
  not_yet_built       — work someone could do inside this framework.
  not_buildable_here  — a limit OF the framework; no work inside it helps. r2's gaps[0] said a wall runner was needed; measured later, at fixed h the wall's only effect is a scalar gamma, which enters no dimensionless group the trap case carries (k* = 21221.4 at all six rungs, identically -- all six are the same dimensionless run, and Faxen lives entirely in the back-transform). No runner there can learn anything about the wall, the same reason a rod's gamma_perp/gamma_par measures 1.000000 in it.
  needs_human_action  — an operator has to do something. No agent closes it.
  needs_data_transfer — the bytes exist, on a machine neither side can reach. AM's P7 is this: the 2026-09-03 drag data lives on the instrument PC under D:\codes, and the repository holds no trajectory data at all. Reading it as `not_yet_built` cost this thread a round of advice premised on the answer being minutes away.
  out_of_scope        — deliberately excluded, not missing.
Optional only so that documents written before this field existed keep validating. R12 warns when it is absent; new gaps should carry it.

would_need.description: What closes it. For `not_buildable_here` this is an alternative METHOD, not a task -- e.g. test the fit procedure on a synthetic gamma(h) rather than report a number from an infinite medium, which is what r1's own `wall_drag` assumption had already asked for. For `needs_data_transfer` name the machine and the path.

owner.description: Who can close it. `nobody` is a valid and important answer -- it is what `not_buildable_here` usually means, and saying so beats leaving a task unassigned.

gaps.description: The experiment side needs this as much as the simulation side, and its absence here was a hole. A precondition written as a checklist item reads closeable; P7 ('run the slope fit on the 2026-09-03 data') reads like a few minutes of work and is in fact a data transfer off an instrument PC. Declare it as a gap with a kind and an owner, so the other side does not plan a round around it.
